copenhagen.workforce: Copenhagen had 378,725 employees in 2025 (real, Statistics Denmark), up from 373,979 in 2024 and 368,220 in 2023 (real, Statistics Denmark). That is growth of about 1.6% in 2024 and about 1.3% in 2025 (real, Statistics Denmark; percentages calculated from these counts), so the rate was slower in the latest year. The data gives total headcounts only, with no breakdown by sector or hours worked.
copenhagen.compare: The data cannot answer this, as it contains no figures for the Hovedstaden region. It does include Frederiksberg, a separate municipality, where employment rose from 56,228 in 2023 to 57,703 in 2025 (real, Statistics Denmark). Over the same period, København's employment rose from 368,220 to 378,725 (real, Statistics Denmark).
copenhagen.rising: Three skills show a rising trend in the synthetic skills data: digital patient records for nurses (confidence 0.72, synthetic), heat-pump installation for electricians (confidence 0.66, synthetic), and electric truck operation for truck drivers (confidence 0.38, synthetic, the lowest of the three). Two other rising skills, offshore wind cable work and highway route planning, come from scenario assumptions rather than observed data, so they are not counted here. The data has no real employment figures by skill.
copenhagen.falling: Only one skill is marked as falling: legacy fuse-box work for electricians (synthetic). The estimate has a confidence score of 0.55 (synthetic) and draws on job ads alone (synthetic), so it is indicative only. The other skills are level or rising (synthetic). Two scenario rows are assumptions, not observed data.
copenhagen.shortage: Nurses and electricians are flagged as being in shortage (synthetic), with ttf values of 62 and 48. Truck drivers are not flagged (synthetic), with a ttf of 35. The file does not define ttf. These are modelled figures, not observed data. The real employment totals (real, Statistics Denmark) are not broken down by occupation, so they cannot confirm these shortages.
copenhagen.completions: The data cannot answer this question: it contains employment counts for København (real, Statistics Denmark) and synthetic skill, shortage and demand indicators, but no training completions or population figures.
copenhagen.scenario: The data contains two scenario assumptions, not observed figures. Offshore wind cable work for electricians is marked rising, with confidence 0.30, based on an assumed offshore wind yard opening (synthetic). Route planning for a rerouted highway for truck drivers is marked rising, with confidence 0.25, based on an assumed government highway reroute (synthetic). Both have low confidence and are what-if cases only.

aarhus.workforce: Aarhus had 197,646 employees in 2025 (real, Statistics Denmark), up from 188,364 in 2023 (real, Statistics Denmark). Growth was about 2.2% from 2023 to 2024 and about 2.7% from 2024 to 2025, both calculated from the real figures. The skills and shortage data are synthetic and give no headcounts, so they cannot size the workforce.
aarhus.compare: The data cannot answer this question because it contains no figures for the Midtjylland region, only for Aarhus. For Aarhus alone, employment rose from 188,364 in 2023 to 197,646 in 2025 (real, Statistics Denmark), and population rose from 361,544 to 373,388 over the same years (real, Statistics Denmark). Education completions edged down from 22,380 to 22,259 (real, Statistics Denmark). A regional comparison would need regional figures.
aarhus.rising: Three skills show a rising trend: cloud infrastructure for software developers (confidence 0.86, synthetic), heat-pump installation (confidence 0.70, synthetic), and automation and data monitoring for process operators (confidence 0.58, synthetic; categorised as transforming). Battery cell operation also shows a rising trend, but this is a scenario assumption (a battery plant opening), not observed data. Manual process control is falling (confidence 0.61, synthetic).
aarhus.falling: Only one skill is marked as falling: manual process control for process operators (synthetic, confidence 0.61, based on job ads and a shortage list). The other skills are rising, transforming or stable. The battery cell operation row is a scenario assumption, not observed data. The skill-level results are all synthetic, so they cannot be checked against official statistics.
aarhus.shortage: Two occupations are flagged as in shortage: Software developers (ttf 88) and Heat-pump installers (ttf 54) (synthetic). Process operators are flagged as not in shortage (ttf 41) (synthetic). These flags are synthetic, not observed data, and the file does not define what "ttf" measures.
aarhus.completions: No. Completions fell from 22,380 in 2023 to 22,259 in 2025 (real, Statistics Denmark), while population rose from 361,544 to 373,388 over the same years (real, Statistics Denmark). That is about 0.5% fewer completions against 3.3% more residents. Completions per 1,000 residents fell from about 61.9 to 59.6 (calculated from real, Statistics Denmark figures). The data has no 2026 completions figure, so it cannot show the latest position.
aarhus.scenario: The only scenario row assumes a battery plant opens, with process operators gaining battery cell operation skills. It is classed as rising, with a confidence of 0.30 (synthetic). These are assumptions, not observed data, so they do not show what has happened in Aarhus. All other skill rows are non-scenario.

odense.workforce: Odense had 105,317 employees in 2025 (real, Statistics Denmark), up from 103,352 in 2024 and 101,961 in 2023 (real, Statistics Denmark). That is growth of about 1.4% in 2024 and about 1.9% in 2025, calculated from those counts (real, Statistics Denmark). The data shows employment rising each year, but it does not explain the causes or break the figures down by sector.
odense.compare: The data has no figures for Region Syddanmark, so Odense cannot be compared with its region. Within Odense, employees rose from 101,961 in 2023 to 105,317 in 2025 (real, Statistics Denmark), population grew from 207,762 to 210,803 over the same years (real, Statistics Denmark), and completions fell from 11,997 to 11,576 (real, Statistics Denmark).
odense.rising: Three skills are marked as rising in the synthetic skills data: data engineering for software developers (synthetic, confidence 0.74), hospital digitisation for nurses (synthetic, confidence 0.55), and telemedicine support for nurses (synthetic, confidence 0.47). None of these comes from observed data. The dataset contains no real skills figures, so it cannot check these trends against Statistics Denmark records. No scenario rows are among the rising skills.
odense.falling: The data shows one skill as falling: fish-processing line operation for fish processors (synthetic, confidence 0.66). Raw-fish handling is also marked falling, but that row is a scenario assumption based on a fishing quota cut, not observed data (synthetic, confidence 0.25). The real figures in the file cover employment, population and completions, not skill trends.
odense.shortage: Two occupations are flagged as in shortage: Nurses (ttf 70) and Software developers (ttf 84) (both synthetic). Fish processors are not flagged, with a ttf of 29 (synthetic). The shortage list is synthetic, not observed data, and the JSON does not define "ttf," so its meaning cannot be confirmed from this data.
odense.completions: No. Completions fell from 11,997 in 2023 to 11,576 in 2025 (real, Statistics Denmark), a drop of about 3.5%. Population rose from 207,762 to 210,803 over the same years (real, Statistics Denmark), an increase of about 1.5%. Completions per 1,000 residents therefore fell from roughly 58 to roughly 55 (calculated from real, Statistics Denmark figures). The data cannot show whether this matches labour-market demand, because the demand and shortage figures are synthetic.
odense.scenario: Only one row is flagged as a scenario, and it is an assumption, not observed data. It assumes that fish processors' raw-fish handling skill falls because of a fishing quota cut (synthetic). Its confidence is 0.25 (synthetic), the lowest of the skill rows (synthetic). The other five skill rows are not scenarios. The scenario does not change any population, employment or completions figures, which are real (real, Statistics Denmark). Read it as a what-if case, not as a description of what has happened.

aalborg.workforce: Aalborg had 115,127 employees in 2025 (real, Statistics Denmark), up from 113,522 in 2024 and 112,226 in 2023 (real, Statistics Denmark). That is growth of about 1.2% in 2024 and 1.4% in 2025, or 2.6% across the two years (calculated from real, Statistics Denmark figures). The data do not explain what is driving this change.
aalborg.compare: The data cannot answer this comparison because it contains no figures for the Nordjylland region. For Aalborg alone, population rose from 222,571 in 2023 to 224,612 in 2025 (real, Statistics Denmark), employees rose from 112,226 to 115,127 over the same period (real, Statistics Denmark), and completions fell from 12,246 to 12,120 (real, Statistics Denmark).
aalborg.rising: Five skill entries show a rising trend in the synthetic skills data (synthetic). Heat-pump installation for electricians has the highest confidence, at 0.69 (synthetic). Heat-pump and air-conditioning service for refrigeration technicians is at 0.63 (synthetic). A second electrician entry, heat-pump installation matched to the shortage list, is at 0.58 (synthetic) and overlaps with the first. Electric truck operation for truck drivers is at 0.44 (synthetic). Ward coordination for nurses is a scenario assumption, not observed data, at 0.20 (synthetic).
aalborg.falling: The synthetic skills data shows one skill falling: manual scaffolding for construction workers (synthetic), with a confidence of 0.52 (synthetic). It comes from job ads only (synthetic). No other skill is marked as falling. The real employment, population and completion figures do not measure skills, so they cannot answer this question.
aalborg.shortage: The synthetic shortage data marks two occupations as on the shortage list: electricians (time-to-fill 51, synthetic) and refrigeration technicians (time-to-fill 57, synthetic). Truck drivers (38, synthetic) and construction workers (33, synthetic) are marked as not on the list. Nurses appear only in a hospital-merger scenario, which is an assumption rather than observed data, so this dataset cannot establish their shortage status.
aalborg.completions: No, not in 2025. Completions fell from 12,416 in 2024 to 12,120 in 2025 (real, Statistics Denmark), while population rose from 223,174 to 224,612 (real, Statistics Denmark). That is about 55.6 completions per 1,000 residents in 2024 and 54.0 in 2025, below the 2023 level of 55.0 (calculated from real, Statistics Denmark figures). The data covers only three years. The skills and shortage figures are synthetic and cannot answer this question.
aalborg.scenario: The only scenario assumption in the data is for nurses: ward coordination after a hospital merger, categorised as transforming with a rising trend. It is based on a hospital merger scenario, not observed data, and the confidence score is low at 0.2 (synthetic). The other skill rows are not scenarios. No real data in the file describes this scenario.

frederiksberg.workforce: Frederiksberg had 57,703 employees in 2025 (real, Statistics Denmark). That is up from 56,879 in 2024 and 56,228 in 2023 (both real, Statistics Denmark). Growth was about 1.2 percent in 2024 and 1.4 percent in 2025, or 2.6 percent over two years (percentages calculated from real, Statistics Denmark, figures). The skills and shortage data are synthetic and do not answer this question.
frederiksberg.compare: The data does not include regional totals for Hovedstaden, so I can only compare Frederiksberg with København, the other municipality in the file. Frederiksberg's employee count rose from 56,228 in 2023 to 57,703 in 2025, about 2.6% (real, Statistics Denmark). København's rose from 368,220 to 378,725 over the same years, about 2.9% (real, Statistics Denmark).
frederiksberg.rising: Two skills are marked as rising, both in synthetic data: cloud infrastructure for software developers, with confidence 0.79 (synthetic), and digital tools and data handling for clerical support workers, with confidence 0.52 (synthetic). Software developers are flagged as in shortage, with a time-to-fill of 72 (synthetic). The skills figures are not real observations, and the dataset contains no real skills measures.
frederiksberg.falling: The data does not show any falling skills. Both skills in the synthetic dataset are marked as rising: cloud infrastructure for software developers (synthetic, confidence 0.79) and digital tools and data handling for clerical support workers (synthetic, confidence 0.52). The data covers only these two skills, so it cannot show whether other skills are declining in Frederiksberg.
frederiksberg.shortage: Only one occupation is flagged as being in shortage: software developers (synthetic). Clerical support workers are not flagged (synthetic). The shortage flags come from a synthetic dataset, not observed records, so they are indicative only. The data does not explain how the "ttf" value is defined, so I cannot say what it measures.
frederiksberg.completions: Not quite. Completions rose from 5,448 in 2023 to 5,595 in 2024, then fell to 5,467 in 2025 (real, Statistics Denmark). Population grew every year, reaching 105,840 in 2025 (real, Statistics Denmark). Completions per 1,000 residents were about 52.0 in 2023, 53.3 in 2024 and 51.7 in 2025 (real, Statistics Denmark, calculated). Output per resident has dropped since 2024 and is slightly below 2023.
frederiksberg.scenario: The data contains no scenario assumptions. Both skill entries are marked as not scenarios and draw on synthetic sources such as job ads (synthetic). For context, employment in Frederiksberg rose from 56,228 in 2023 to 57,703 in 2025 (real, Statistics Denmark).

lolland.workforce: The workforce was 15,487 employees in 2025 (real, Statistics Denmark), down from 15,585 in 2023 (real, Statistics Denmark). That is a fall of 98 employees, about 0.6%, over two years, with the same loss of 49 each year. Population also declined over this period, from 39,921 to 39,122 (real, Statistics Denmark). The data contain no workforce projections.
lolland.compare: The data cannot answer a full regional comparison because it contains no figures for Region Sjælland as a whole. It does compare Lolland with Guldborgsund. In 2025, Lolland had 39,122 residents and 15,487 employees (real, Statistics Denmark), while Guldborgsund had 59,350 residents and 25,829 employees (real, Statistics Denmark). Lolland recorded 956 completions, against 1,748 in Guldborgsund (real, Statistics Denmark).
lolland.rising: Heat-pump installation is the only observed skill marked as rising in Lolland, with confidence of 0.57 (synthetic). Its occupation is also flagged as in shortage, with a time-to-fill figure of 50 (synthetic). Tunnel construction for the Femern link is also marked rising, but this is a scenario assumption, not observed data, and confidence is low at 0.3 (synthetic). Manual process control is marked as falling, with confidence of 0.64 (synthetic).
lolland.falling: Only one skill is marked as falling: manual process control for process operators, with a confidence score of 0.64 (synthetic). The synthetic demand index for process operators rises across its three values, from 79 to 100 (synthetic), and the occupation is not flagged as short of workers, with a time-to-fill figure of 35 (synthetic). Total employment in the municipality fell from 15,585 in 2023 to 15,487 in 2025 (real, Statistics Denmark). The data does not show a skill-level employment trend.
lolland.shortage: Two occupations are flagged as in shortage: Construction workers (ttf 58) and Heat-pump installers (ttf 50) (both synthetic). Process operators are not flagged (ttf 35) (synthetic). The Construction workers flag sits alongside a Femern link tunnel-construction row, which is a scenario assumption rather than observed data, with confidence 0.3 (synthetic). The data does not state the criteria used for the shortage list.
lolland.completions: No, completions are falling faster than population. Completions dropped from 1,033 in 2023 to 956 in 2025 (real, Statistics Denmark), about 7.5%. Population fell from 39,921 to 39,122 over the same period (real, Statistics Denmark), about 2%. Completions per 1,000 residents therefore slipped from about 25.9 to 24.4 (calculated from real, Statistics Denmark figures). The data does not include training capacity or enrolment, so it cannot explain the cause.
lolland.scenario: The only scenario row assumes rising demand for tunnel construction skills linked to the Femern link, for construction workers. This is an assumption, not observed data, with a confidence of 0.3 (synthetic). The same occupation is flagged as in shortage with a time-to-fill of 58 (synthetic), but the data does not show whether the scenario contributed to that figure.

guldborgsund.workforce: Guldborgsund had 25,829 employees in 2025 (real, Statistics Denmark), down from 25,942 in 2023 (real, Statistics Denmark). The workforce fell by 63 in 2024 and by 50 in 2025, about 0.4% in total over two years, with the annual decline slightly smaller in 2025. The skills and demand data are synthetic and do not measure headcount.
guldborgsund.compare: The data has no regional total for Sjælland, so the only comparison is with Lolland. Guldborgsund is larger: its population fell from 60,231 in 2023 to 59,119 in 2026 (real, Statistics Denmark), while Lolland's fell from 39,921 to 38,533 (real, Statistics Denmark). Employee numbers declined slightly in both areas over 2023 to 2025 (real, Statistics Denmark). Guldborgsund recorded 1,748 completions in 2025, against 956 in Lolland (real, Statistics Denmark). Both show falling process-operator and rising heat-pump installer trends (synthetic). Lolland's construction-worker trend is a scenario assumption, not observed data.
guldborgsund.rising: Only one skill is marked as rising in the data: heat-pump installation, for heat-pump installers (synthetic, job ads, confidence 0.61). Manual process control is falling (synthetic, confidence 0.58), and elderly care is level (synthetic, confidence 0.74). These are synthetic job-ad signals, not observed statistics, so treat them as indicative only.
guldborgsund.falling: Only one skill is marked as falling: manual process control, linked to process operators (synthetic, based on job ads). Its confidence score is 0.58 (synthetic), which is moderate. The data does not show how large the decline is. For comparison, heat-pump installation is rising and elderly care is level (both synthetic).
guldborgsund.shortage: The data does not include a shortage list for Guldborgsund, as the shortage section is empty. It does contain synthetic job-ad trends for three occupations, which show skill demand rather than official shortage status. Heat-pump installers are rising (confidence 0.61, synthetic), process operators are falling (confidence 0.58, synthetic), and nurses are level (confidence 0.74, synthetic).
guldborgsund.completions: No, not in 2025. Completions per 1,000 residents were about 32.0 in 2023 and 32.4 in 2024, then fell to about 29.4 in 2025 (calculated from real, Statistics Denmark, figures). Completions dropped from 1,935 to 1,748 between 2024 and 2025, while population fell from 59,759 to 59,350 (both real, Statistics Denmark). The data does not explain the drop. The skills and demand figures are synthetic and do not cover completions.
guldborgsund.scenario: The data contains no scenario assumptions. All three skill rows for Guldborgsund are marked as not scenarios. They show heat-pump installation rising (synthetic, confidence 0.61), manual process control falling (synthetic, confidence 0.58), and elderly care staying level (synthetic, confidence 0.74). All three come from job ads (synthetic). The shortage and demand index sections are empty, so they add no scenario figures.

naestved.workforce: Næstved had 41,126 employees in 2025 (real, Statistics Denmark), up from 40,915 in 2024 and 40,690 in 2023 (real, Statistics Denmark). Growth eased slightly: employees rose by 225 in 2024, about 0.6 percent, and by 211 in 2025, about 0.5 percent (real, Statistics Denmark). Over the two years the total increase was 436, about 1.1 percent (real, Statistics Denmark).
naestved.compare: The data has no regional totals for Sjælland, so this compares Næstved with Lolland only. From 2023 to 2025, Næstved's employees rose from 40,690 to 41,126, about 1.1%, while Lolland's fell about 0.6% (real, Statistics Denmark). Næstved's population grew about 0.4%, while Lolland's fell about 2.0% (real, Statistics Denmark). Completions fell in both: about 2.8% in Næstved and 7.5% in Lolland (real, Statistics Denmark). Skill trends are synthetic. Lolland's construction worker trend is a scenario assumption, not observed data.
naestved.rising: Three skills show a rising trend in the synthetic job-ad data (synthetic): cloud infrastructure for software developers (confidence 0.55, synthetic), digital patient records for nurses (confidence 0.66, synthetic; categorised as transforming), and heat-pump installation for electricians (confidence 0.48, synthetic). These are modest confidence levels, so treat them as indicative. The dataset holds no real skills figures for Næstved.
naestved.falling: None of the three skills in the data is marked as falling. Cloud infrastructure, digital patient records and heat-pump installation are all recorded as rising (synthetic, based on job ads). The data covers only these three skills, so it cannot show whether other skills are falling in Næstved.
naestved.shortage: The data does not answer this question because the shortage section is empty. It does include synthetic job-ad data on skill trends for software developers, nurses and electricians (synthetic), but these describe skills, not shortages.
naestved.completions: Not in 2025. Completions fell from 3,157 in 2024 to 3,030 in 2025 (real, Statistics Denmark), while population rose from 84,747 to 84,895 (real, Statistics Denmark). That is about 35.7 completions per 1,000 residents, down from 37.3 in 2024 and 36.9 in 2023 (real, Statistics Denmark; ratios calculated from these figures). The data has no 2026 completions, so it cannot show whether this pattern continues.
naestved.scenario: The data contains no scenario assumptions. All three skill entries are marked as not scenarios and come from job ads (synthetic): cloud infrastructure for software developers (rising, confidence 0.55, synthetic), digital patient records for nurses (transforming, confidence 0.66, synthetic), and heat-pump installation for electricians (rising, confidence 0.48, synthetic). The shortage and demand index sections are empty.
